strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing the accuracy-interpretability tradeoff with clear conceptual distinction between global (MEM) and local explanations
Solid technical framework with clever architectural design (guj(0)=0, x-j masking) ensuring linear coefficient interpretability while enabling nonlinear corrections
Novel application of parameter elimination for joint optimization of linear coefficients and NN parameters, with principled extension to adaptive ridge regression
Comprehensive and well-designed experimental evaluation including synthetic data with ground truth, multiple strong baselines, extensive ablations, and reproducibility details
Generally clear presentation with informative figures, well-organized structure, and thorough supplementary materials
weaknesses: Significant architectural limitation: inability to capture self-interactions (x²j, etc.) due to constraint that guj depends only on x-j; workaround requires feature engineering, undermining interpretability benefits

Weak real-world evaluation: on 3 datasets tested, NIMO achieves only comparable (not superior) performance to baselines; diabetes shows no clear advantage, Boston/superconductivity match standard methods, providing limited evidence of practical value

Marginal Effects at Mean (MEM) limitations inadequately addressed: Table 2 shows MEM diverges from SHAP rankings on Boston housing; explanation via 'feature selection instability' raises questions about whether MEM captures meaningful stable interpretations

Interpretability evaluation not rigorous: paper focuses heavily on predictive performance; lacks systematic comparison of interpretability quality across methods and does not validate that NIMO's interpretations are more meaningful/stable than alternatives

Limited novelty: combines existing techniques (hybrid models, parameter elimination via profile likelihood, adaptive ridge regression); main contribution is specific architectural choice, which is somewhat incremental

Missing theoretical and empirical guidance: no characterization of when NIMO outperforms alternatives, no analysis of approximation quality, no convergence guarantees, and no sensitivity analysis for hyperparameter choices
Implementation-theory gap: theoretical model uses d separate networks but implementation uses single shared network with positional encoding plus noise injection (workaround for sparsity enforcement)

Experimental concerns: no statistical significance testing in Table 1; inconsistent baseline performance (e.g., NAM underperforms Lasso on synthetic additive data despite designed for this setting) deserves explanation
